S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (PDD), or dysthymia, is a chronic depressive condition characterized by a low mood lasting at least two years in adults, with accompanying cognitive, emotional, and somatic features that are less intense than major depressive episodes but more enduring. Individuals often describe themselves as having always been this way, and the disorder may be punctuated by superimposed major depressive episodes (“double depression”). Functioning is typically maintained at a basic level, but with significant subjective distress, reduced productivity, and impaired quality of life in work, relationships, and self-care. It is differentiated from major depressive disorder primarily by its chronicity and trait-like course, and from cyclothymia or bipolar disorders by the absence of hypomanic or manic episodes.

patient.personality: Phillip is a steady, meticulous supervisor who enjoys quiet, nature-focused hobbies and careful planning, sometimes to the point of over-scheduling himself.
patient.stressor: About two years and a few months ago, Phillip developed a persistent back and shoulder strain after a season of long hours supervising a major expansion in the agricultural operation, which forced him to cut back on some of the physical work he prided himself on and rely more on others for tasks he used to handle himself. The lingering discomfort, multiple medical visits, and advice to limit certain activities made him feel less capable at work and at home, and he slowly stopped going on longer hikes, doing woodworking projects, and volunteering as often for conservation outings. Over time, the combination of ongoing pain, disrupted sleep, and the sense that he could no longer keep up with the demands of both the fields and his own high standards wore him down, and his days began to feel like an exhausting grind despite his attempts to over-plan and compensate. He finally sought psychiatric help after his spouse pointed out that his constant tiredness and disengagement were affecting family life and that he had been in this depleted state for more than two years without improvement despite resolving most of the acute physical injury.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m exhausted all the time, no matter how much I rest, and I just don’t have any energy left for anything.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: For a long time now I wake up feeling low and sort of hollow inside, like the day’s already a loss before I even get out of bed, and even being out in the fields or the woods—which used to lift my mood—just feels kind of dull and gray now instead of peaceful or satisfying.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how early I go to bed or how much I try to rest my back and shoulders, I drag myself through the day like I’m walking in mud, coming home so wiped out that even simple things like fixing a loose hinge or going for a short walk with my wife feel like too much effort.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: I used to be sharp with planning out the crews and the planting schedule, but now my head feels foggy all the time—I find myself staring at the clipboard, second-guessing every little decision and forgetting things I just told someone five minutes earlier.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: Honestly, I don’t really see this getting better anymore; I just figure this tired, worn-down version of me is how it’s going to be from here on out, no matter what the doctors or my wife say.
